traits.ribs.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (read on eFloras 2026-10-19), : Peniocereus greggii: shrubs, erect to sprawling, usually inconspicuous; stems gray-green to gray, simple or with 2-5 branches, 40-120(-300) cm, distally 8-20 mm in diameter, about 10 mm at midlength; ribs 4-6, prominent; areoles (3.5-)12(-15) mm apart. Spines (9-)11-15(-17) per areole, the abaxial 3-5 appressed, yellowish white throughout or only at the tips, to 3 mm; the adaxial black, subulate, to 1 mm. Flowers nocturnal, 15-25 cm; outer tepals greenish white with brown to reddish midstripes; inner tepals white or lightly tinged cream or pink, lanceolate-attenuate, 4-7 cm; anthers cream-yellow; style white, 10-14 cm; stigma lobes 9-11, white. Fruits bright red, ellipsoid, 60-90 × 40-50 mm. Var. greggii: flowers 15-17 × 5-6 cm, flowering late spring, fruiting summer; var. transmontanus: flowers 22-25 × 7-8 cm, flowering spring-summer, fruiting summer-early fall. Colours by hand from the words; the carpels as many as the stigma lobes; the months of both varieties, late spring to summer, and their fruit summer to early autumn; the floral tube the flower's 15-25 cm less its 4-7 cm tepals, rounded down to 10-16 cm.
